metadata.title: Expanded 12x14 Architectural-Algorithmic Compatibility Matrix
metadata.academic_grounding: Luo & Han CASCADE (19x15), Jacob PromptShield (Low-FPR <=1%), NIST AI RMF, ISO/IEC/IEEE 42010

evaluations.justification: Deterministic string matching lacks continuous margin z for Platt calibration.
No language model distribution to compute token perplexity.
Native domain: Regex directly decodes homoglyphs, zero-width, base64, and leetspeak.
No continuous metric space representation.
No internal neural layers or activations.
No attention matrices to decouple content and position.
Non-differentiable rules cannot optimize KL divergence invariant loss.
Perturbation breaks exact string signatures, creating massive false negatives.
Discrete non-differentiable rules cannot compute minimax gradients.
Only binary outputs {0, 1}; lacks continuous risk scores for tri-state conformal partitioning.
Fixed binary rules produce discrete ROC steps, cannot smoothly interpolate low-FPR.
Can detect and sanitize delimiters (XML/Markdown tags) prior to model ingestion.
Executes fast head/tail string truncation and regex regex scan in < 0.1ms.
Stateless regex cannot track semantic drift trajectories across conversational turns.
Binary hash lookups do not map to continuous TF-IDF vector margins.
No language model probabilities.
Detects forbidden tokens, but homoglyphs cause false negative hash misses.
Exact hash keys cannot measure continuous cosine distance.
No neural activations.
No attention mechanism.
Non-trainable static dictionary.
Stochastic noise causes hash lookup misses.
Non-differentiable hash table.
Cannot calibrate risk thresholds on deterministic hash hit/miss.
Step-function ROC curve with high false positive trigger rates.
Can enforce prohibited keyword blacklists on specific prompt fields.
O(1) hash lookups on 200k char chunks execute in sub-millisecond time.
Stateless dictionary matching cannot model multi-turn contextual accumulation.
Native core: Sublinear word TF-IDF + Platt logistic margin produces optimal calibrated scores in 1.2ms.
Requires auxiliary n-gram LM; adds latency overhead to sub-millisecond inference.
Word-level n-grams are vulnerable to character mutations and leetspeak.
Sparse centroids in 50k-dim space suffer from sparsity and curse of dimensionality.
Linear model has no deep hidden states or attention gradients.
Lacks self-attention mechanism.
Linear weights lack capacity to absorb KL invariant loss without massive accuracy drop.
Running M=10 iterations multiplies latency to 12ms, defeating fast filter purpose.
Discrete vocabulary requires greedy coordinate ascent rather than continuous SGD.
Platt calibrated output perfectly supports Conformal Risk Control to partition traffic at FPR < 1.5%.
Continuous logistic margin enables clean ROC threshold interpolation down to FPR 0.5%.
Can train separate weight heads for system vs user prompt sections.
Super-fast linear scoring (<0.1ms/block) enables real-time scanning of 200k documents with early stopping.
Can concatenate past turn TF-IDF vectors, but lacks semantic nuance.
Combines character n-gram frequencies (3-5 chars) with linear/kernel decision margins.
Char-level perplexity can be approximated but adds computation overhead.
Native champion for typographical anomaly: char_wb captures leetspeak, punctuation obfuscation, and typos.
High-dimensional sparse char n-gram centroids suffer from sparsity.
Linear SVM has no deep internal activations.
No self-attention mechanism.
Convex SVM formulation does not naturally accommodate MOF KL loss.
Inherent robustness to character perturbation makes randomized smoothing partially redundant.
Adversarial training via greedy char flips improves boundary robustness.
Platt/Isotonic calibrated SVM margins allow finite-sample CRC risk bounding.
Allows fine-grained threshold interpolation in the low-FPR regime.
Can weight character n-grams from privileged fields differently.
Fast feature extraction (<0.2ms/block) makes it ideal for Tier 1 block scanning of long documents.
Limited context retention across multi-turn sessions.
Random Forest outputs tree vote probabilities, but uncalibrated leaf distributions require isotonic regression.
Inefficient for sequence probability modeling.
Captures non-linear feature interactions but memory scales poorly with char n-grams.
Tree partitioning differs from metric distance spaces.
No continuous hidden representations.
No attention mechanism.
Tree splits are non-differentiable; cannot optimize continuous MOF KL loss.
Bagging already provides variance reduction; extra smoothing inflates CPU latency to 40ms.
Non-differentiable trees make continuous adversarial optimization difficult.
Tree probabilities can be conformalized but suffer from step discontinuities.
Step-wise ROC curves make extreme low-FPR interpolation sub-optimal (Ayub CAMLIS 2024).
Requires hand-crafted feature engineering for instruction hierarchies.
Tree inference is slower than linear models (3-5ms/block), causing latency accumulation on 200k docs.
Concatenating multi-turn trees causes exponential feature explosion.
Concatenating dense embeddings with sparse TF-IDF is redundant and memory-heavy.
Bi-encoders output pooled vectors, not autoregressive next-token distributions.
Sentence embeddings partially smooth out character anomalies, blinding the model to unicode tricks.
Native design (Ayub [21]): Cosine distance to toxic cluster centroids in continuous R^384.
Can extract intermediate layer embeddings, but pooling discards token-level trajectories.
Uses standard Multi-Head Attention without content-position disentanglement.
Contrastive loss can enforce invariance, but lacks token-level MOF attribution.
Averaging M=10 dense vectors is mathematically sound but inflates CPU latency to 80ms.
Continuous vector space allows Projected Gradient Descent (PGD) in embedding space.
Cosine proximity scores map smoothly into [0, 1] for empirical Conformal Risk Control.
Dense clustering yields smooth ROC, but hubness problem causes high false positive floor (10-15%).
Cross-attention between privileged and untrusted prompt is absent in bi-encoders.
Embedding 50 blocks of 512 tokens requires 400ms on CPU, violating low-latency constraints.
Cosine similarity between turn vectors tracks semantic drift trajectory cleanly.
Linear probes operate on continuous hidden dimensions, not external TF-IDF features.
Hidden state norms correlate with perplexity spikes.
Subword tokenizers fragment character anomalies before reaching hidden layers.
Probes measure separation of hidden vectors across instruction-following regimes.
Native domain (InstructDetector [19], RAP-ID [29]): Probing residual stream activations and attention entropy.
Evaluates internal attention weights, but does not restructure the underlying attention formula.
Can penalize trigger-sensitive hidden neurons during probe training.
Hidden state variance under perturbation measures model stability.
Adversarial gradients can be backpropagated directly to probe representations.
Probe logits can be calibrated using conformal prediction.
Provides smooth ROC curves for low-FPR tuning.
Explicitly measures how privileged system instructions are overwritten in hidden layers.
Requires full forward passes of underlying LLM, making 200k char scanning prohibitively slow.
Tracks representation shifts across multiple conversational forward passes.
Deep self-attention renders external bag-of-words TF-IDF obsolete and redundant.
Pseudo-Perplexity via Masked LM is effective but requires N forward passes (>100ms).
Subword BPE/WordPiece tokenization is blinded by character mutations (Hackett [31]).
[CLS] token pooling suffers from representation anisotropy (narrow cone collapse).
Can probe intermediate layers, though later layers suffer from trigger word over-fitting.
Absolute position embeddings are added to token embeddings at layer 0; cannot disentangle relative vectors.
MOF loss on output logits helps, but fixed absolute position limits semantic decoupling.
SmoothLLM M=10 inflates latency from 35ms to 350ms on CPU.
FGM / FreeLB adversarial training on token embeddings significantly hardens BERT.
Softmax risk scores are readily calibrated via Conformal Risk Control.
Supports ROC interpolation, but trigger word bias creates false positive bumps at low FPR.
Segment embeddings (token_type_ids) provide rudimentary two-level privilege separation.
Scanning 200k chars requires ~40 forward passes, taking ~1.2s on CPU without early stopping.
Cross-turn attention is bounded by 512 token context window.
Disentangled attention captures full contextual semantics; TF-IDF is redundant inside M9.
RTD discriminator scores flag replaced tokens, acting as a learned perplexity proxy.
Subword tokenizer requires Tier-0 Heuristic Scrubber to prevent unicode blindness.
Produces less anisotropic embeddings than BERT, though end-to-end classification is superior.
Intermediate disentangled representations provide clean gradient signals for probing.
Sovereign Champion: Decouples content and relative position across 3 attention matrices (He ICLR 2023).
Sovereign Champion: MOF KL loss (Li ACL 2025) eliminates keyword trigger bias while preserving F1 > 0.95.
SmoothLLM is redundant due to MOF robustness, and M=10 raises latency to 250ms.
Sovereign Champion: Minimax optimization (DataSentinel) hardens DeBERTa against adaptive evasion.
Sovereign Champion: Finite-sample CRC calibrates softmax output to rigorously bound FPR <= 1.5%.
Produces smooth, monotonic ROC curves achieving TPR >= 90% at FPR <= 1.0% (PromptShield criteria).
Relative position attention cleanly preserves boundary distinctions between system and user prompts.
Combined with Tier 1 Early-Stopping, M9 only inspects ambiguous tail/head blocks, keeping latency < 25ms.
High-capacity representation models multi-turn prompt context within 512 token budget.
Multilingual tokenizer and self-attention supersede statistical n-grams.
Cross-lingual token prediction acts as multilingual perplexity filter.
Larger vocabulary (250k tokens) captures diverse scripts, though unicode evasion still requires Tier 0.
Cross-lingual semantic clustering maps Vietnamese and English attacks to shared manifolds.
Cross-lingual alignment can be inspected via hidden state probes.
Disentangled attention generalises across diverse word-order typologies (SVO vs SOV).
MOF loss prevents over-defense on translated sensitive keywords across languages (Deng ICLR 2024).
Perturbation in low-resource languages can shift tokens out-of-vocabulary.
Cross-lingual minimax optimization hardens model against multilingual code-switching evasion.
CRC provides separate calibration thresholds per language to guarantee global FPR <= 1.5%.
Maintains high TPR under low-FPR constraints across both English and Vietnamese.
Enforces privilege boundaries across mixed-language prompts.
Protects long translated documents via block chunking with early stopping.
Tracks conversational language-switching drift across multiple turns.
FlashAttention-2 and RoPE make external statistical features completely redundant.
Can compute sequence likelihood over extended context.
Standard subword tokenizer requires front-end heuristic scrubbing.
Global pooled embeddings capture document-level semantic representations.
GeGLU activations provide rich non-linear hidden representations for probing.
Uses Rotary Position Embeddings (RoPE); structurally different from DeBERTa disentanglement but solves relative position.
MOF invariant loss applies directly to 8,192 token classification head.
Smoothing across 8k tokens is computationally expensive.
FlashAttention enables fast adversarial gradient computation over long contexts.
Conformal Risk Control calibrates long-context document risk scores directly.
Enables precise ROC threshold interpolation for long RAG documents.
Native 8,192 window allows end-to-end modeling of complex system prompts, RAG context, and user input.
Sovereign Champion: Native 8,192 window eliminates the need for block chunking on documents up to 32k characters!
Fits entire multi-turn conversation histories (10+ turns) in a single forward pass without sliding window truncation.
TF-IDF is obsolete for 2B-8B autoregressive generative language models.
Native champion: Autoregressive causal decoder computes exact token perplexity in a single forward pass.
Slow token-by-token generation is ineffective for surface character anomaly detection.
Causal unidirectional attention produces poor sentence-level metric embeddings.
Hidden states can be probed, but generative reasoning is the primary output.
Decoder-only LLMs use standard RoPE / causal attention, incompatible with 3-matrix disentanglement.
Can use DPO/RLHF to reduce over-defense, but fine-tuning requires massive compute.
Disastrous Latency: M=10 perturbations on an 8B model takes 15-20 SECONDS, paralyzing real-time ingress.
Minimax adversarial training on 8B LLMs requires massive multi-GPU compute clusters.
Conformal prediction on safety verdict tokens ('Safe'/'Unsafe') provides rigorous high-assurance risk bounds.
Token log-probabilities allow threshold interpolation, but latency restricts real-time tuning.
Native reasoning: Understands complex instruction hierarchies via in-context policy reasoning.
Scanning 200k documents by chunking into an 8B model incurs enormous GPU memory and tens of seconds latency.
Native multi-turn reasoning: Full causal attention models subtle Crescendo escalation trajectories across turns.
